doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Listening to If You Could See Me Now
summary: They play Austin Cromer singing her arrangement, and Bryant asks whether Dizzy suggested the tune.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We’re going to change the format here a little bit, Melba, and do – let’s hear some music, some of your arrangements, and we’re going to comment on it. First thing I want to hear, Austin Cromer sings your arrangement of If You Could See Me Now. That was great. [The music plays.] How did you write that arrangement, Melba? Oh man, and sit through them playing it like that? Isn’t that a thrill? Do you get thrilled when you hear your arrangements?
Just sometimes? This should have been one of the times.
I watch you getting thrilled, and then I get a thrill from that.

Because after you guys had done that, now who was it that came over and I played this and your Reverie and Annie’s Dance and everything, and you should have seen the expressions on the whole – I’m trying to think who it was that they were – that came over. I was always there with somebody – somebody out of Basie’s band, and we were playing that music. That was beautiful. What gave you the – who suggested that tune?
I guess he did. I wrote it. I don’t know. I don’t think Dizzy had anything to do with it.
